audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was given to Karma while whys[4] on the same row says Irelia's ult-plus-stun all-in kills through a spent shield, and 2+ items was given to Irelia while whys[6] says the duel 'sits roughly even'.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Karma, Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Skill, and the Emerald+ win rate here is 36.73%. Karma gains nothing at 6 — Mantra is live from level 1 — while Irelia gains Vanguard's Edge, a 950-range ult that leaves a slowing wall across her escape.
audit.corrected: Row 4 -> Irelia and row 6 -> Skill in both layers as one atomic pair group, with both phase whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 phase said only 'No new ultimate at 6... His spike is the danger window', naming neither Irelia's ult nor what it does, and used the wrong pronoun for Karma.
audit.why: Vanguard's Edge marks everyone it hits and then forms a wall that damages and slows anyone walking through it — which is exactly the escape Karma's Inspire speed was supposed to buy. That is the reason the row is Irelia's, and it is the fact the reader needs.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Vanguard's Edge cutting the Inspire escape and restates Mantra's level-1 availability.
sources: kit: Irelia R 'the blades form a wall that will damage and slow enemies that walk through it'

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Defiant Dance 'heals back the damage' and blocks Karma's burst in whys[5], spikes[3] and wants.foe[2]. Both halves are wrong, and the second half is dangerous: it tells a magic-damage champion her poke is being reduced when it is not.
audit.why: Riot's text for Defiant Dance: 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge' — no healing, and physical only, so it does nothing against Inner Flame or the Mantra-Q cataclysm. The healing in her kit is Bladesurge, which heals her on every reset. Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s at 850 range.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance restated as a physical-only damage cut, the healing reattributed to Bladesurge, the 16s/850 numbers written into the do's, and the Vanguard's Edge wall added to the don'ts. Soulflare replaced with Mantra-Q in whys[0], spikes[0] and wants.you[0].
sources: kit: Irelia W 'takes reduced physical damage during the charge', cd 20/18/16/14/12
kit: Irelia Q heal flag + reset text

edits.before: No new ultimate at 6 — your Mantra has been online since level 1. His spike is the danger window: respect it.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge walls off your Inspire escape and her stun all-ins you — Mantra was live from level 1.

edits.before: You drift toward utility now — peel, shield, and speed your carries while the RQ poke softens objectives.
edits.after: Neither of you solos the other — peel with the root, speed your carries, never side-lane into her alone.

edits.before: Her Trinity Force spike plus stacked passive attack speed grinds through your Inspire shield faster than your Inner Flame poke can wear her down, and Defiant Dance heals back the damage, so she wins every extended trade.
edits.after: Her Trinity Force spike plus stacked passive attack speed grinds through your Inspire shield faster than your Inner Flame wears her down, and Bladesurge heals her on every reset, so she wins extended trades.

edits.before: Channel Defiant Dance (W) through your Inner Flame poke to block the burst and heal, then snowball off the first kill
edits.after: Charge Defiant Dance for the bigger strike — its damage cut is physical only, so it does nothing to your Inner Flame

edits.before: Her Trinity Force spike turns every Bladesurge reset into a Sheen-boosted auto, and her stacked passive attack speed grinds through a single Inspire shield in one trade — you can't poke her down faster than she heals it back with Defiant Dance.
edits.after: Her Trinity Force spike turns every Bladesurge reset into a Sheen-boosted auto, and her stacked passive attack speed grinds through a single Inspire shield in one trade — you cannot poke her down faster than Bladesurge resets heal her back.

edits.before: Mantra is up from level 1, so RQ Soulflare threatens real poke before she has any minions for Bladesurge to dash through — the one stage she can't flicker out of your slow zone.
edits.after: Mantra is up from level 1, so Mantra-Q threatens real poke before she has any minions for Bladesurge to dash through — the one stage she cannot flicker out of your zone.

edits.before: Open RQ Soulflare the instant she walks up to last-hit — before she has a minion wave, Bladesurge has nothing to dash off, so this is the only stage she can't flicker out of your slow zone. Chunk her here.
edits.after: Open Mantra-Q the instant she walks up to last-hit — before she has a minion wave, Bladesurge has nothing to dash off, so this is the only stage she cannot flicker out of your slow zone. Chunk her here.

edits.before: Land Level 1 RQ Soulflare before she has a minion wave to Bladesurge-reset through your slow zone
edits.after: Land the level-1 Mantra-Q before she has a minion wave to Bladesurge-reset through your slow zone

edits.before: Her stun setup — dodge it and the dive falls apart. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1 from 850 — dodge the converge and the whole dive falls apart.

edits.before: That’s Irelia’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge leaves a wall behind you — you have no dash, so hold Flash for it.
